title: COUNT(*) inflated the session count
description: Fix the query so it returns every database and the actual number of related sessions, including 0 for a database with no sessions. Return exactly two columns: database_name, session_count. Sort by session_count DESC, then database_name ASC.
starter_sql:
SELECT d.name AS database_name, COUNT(*) AS session_count
FROM databases AS d
LEFT JOIN sessions AS s ON s.database_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.name
ORDER BY session_count DESC, d.name ASC;
hints: LEFT JOIN still creates one NULL-extended row for a database without sessions.
Count a non-NULL key from the right table instead of *.
solution_explanation: COUNT(s.id) ignores the NULL-extended LEFT JOIN row and therefore returns 0 correctly.
